The elections coincided with the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 U.S. presidential election]], as well as [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2024 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]], and various [[2024 United States elections|state and local elections]]. When the results were updated on July 10, Maloy was ahead of Jenkins by only 219 votes, which was less than 0.25% of the total vote, the threshold for which the state initiates an automatic recount.{{cite news |last1=Lesniewski |first1=Niels |title=Maloy's slim lead in Utah House race heading to recount |work=[[Roll Call]] |date=July 10, 2024 |url=https://rollcall.com/2024/07/10/maloys-slim-lead-in-utah-house-race-heading-to-recount/}} Jenkins officially asked for a recount on July 29.{{cite web |last1=Tomco |first1=Brigham |title=Colby Jenkins requests recount in Utah's 2nd District race against Rep. Celeste Maloy |url=https://www.deseret.com/utah/2024/07/29/utah-2nd-district-primary-recount/ |publisher=[[Deseret News]] |access-date=31 July 2024 |date=29 July 2024}} ===Democratic primary=== Brian Adams was the only Democrat to file. He faced backlash from fellow Democrats for his [[anti-abortion]] beliefs, his opposition to president [[Joe Biden]] and support for independent presidential candidate [[Robert F. Kennedy Jr.]], and for describing convicted [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6 Capitol attack]] participants as "politically persecuted." As a result, Adams withdrew after receiving the Democratic nomination. Democratic central committee members in the 2nd district met to choose a replacement nominee on May 25. Out of eight candidates, committee members chose lawyer Nathaniel Woodward after five rounds of [[instant-runoff voting|ranked-choice voting]]. In the final round, Woodward defeated the runner-up, Garret Rushforth, by just 1 vote. ====Withdrew after nomination==== *Brian Adams, renewable energy consultant{{cite news |access-date=May 5, 2024 |work=[[KSL-TV]] |url=https://www.ksl.com/article/51000100/democratic-congressional-candidate-in-utah-withdraws-after-defending-jan-6-participants |date=May 2, 2024 |author=Beal-Cvetko, Bridger |title=Democratic congressional candidate in Utah withdraws after defending Jan. 6 participants}} ====Replacement nominee==== *Nathaniel Woodward, chair of the [[Carbon County, Utah|Carbon County]] Democratic Party{{cite news |access-date=May 30, 2024 |work=[[Utah News Dispatch]] |url=https://www.standard.net/news/government/2024/may/28/carbon-county-attorney-is-the-democratic-partys-choice-for-utahs-2nd-congressional-district/ |date=May 28, 2024 |author=Cabrera, Alixel |title=Carbon County attorney is the Democratic Party's choice for Utah's 2nd Congressional District}} ====Not nominated==== *Benjamin Coffey, project engineer *Darrell Curtis, former nonprofit employee *Charles Free, cab driver *Randy Hopkins, retired Utah Department of Workforce Services regional director and candidate for this district in [[2018 United States House of Representatives elections in Utah#District 2|2018]] and [[2020 United States House of Representatives elections in Utah#District 2|2020]] *Schuyler Rhodes, chair of the [[Iron County, Utah|Iron County]] Democratic Party *Garret Rushforth, teacher{{cite news |access-date=May 30, 2024 |author=Cabrera, Alixel |work=[[Utah News Dispatch]] |url=https://utahnewsdispatch.com/2024/05/23/candidates-utah-democratic-party-2nd-congressional-district/ |date=May 23, 2024 |title=Democrats have a spot to fill in the race for Utah's 2nd Congressional District.
